ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Tabarak Isma Rabbika' in Shia supplications?
ai.summary: This phrase, derived from Surah Ar-Rahman (55:78), serves as a cornerstone of Shia liturgical remembrance, often recited to invoke divine blessings and acknowledge God's supreme majesty and generosity. It is deeply embedded in daily supplications and funeral rites, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual potency of God's name as a means of connecting with the Divine. The invocation highlights the dual attributes of awe (Jalal) and grace (Ikram), central to understanding God's relationship with creation in Shia theology.
